item.text: {"question_id":"6B.10","answer":"The evidence does not establish that ordinary people, including disadvantaged groups, ended the 2019–2023 period with durably better life chances than inherited. There were government-linked improvements in access and institutional capacity: free public primary education was implemented from 2019, with enrollment rising substantially by 2021–2022, and the government reported continuing PDL-145T construction of schools and health centres in 2023 (BATCH-0012-R01-E019; BATCH-0014-E004; BATCH-0023-E001). UNDP-supported justice reforms also expanded magistrate staffing and access to justice in 2023, while government-reported services for survivors of gender-based violence included integrated centres, clinics, legal support and assistance to 9,500 women (BATCH-0009-E004; BATCH-0011-E006). These are attributable or government-linked implementation outputs, but they are partly donor-supported, incompletely independently verified, and do not by themselves demonstrate durable, broad life-chance gains. Free maternity care became effective only in September 2023; its reported beneficiary total covers the following year, so it should not be treated as a completed 2023 outcome (BATCH-0020-E005). Against these gains, tenure-level and 2023 evidence shows severe and unequal conditions: crisis or emergency food insecurity nearly doubled to nearly 26 million during the tenure, more than 60% of the population lived below $2.15 per day, displacement reached roughly seven million, and preschool attendance remained about 5% with more than 7.5 million children out of school (BATCH-0028-E020). In 2023 specifically, more than 25 million people faced crisis or emergency food insecurity, 6.8 million were internally displaced by year-end, inflation was reported at 33.9% at year-end, and insecurity had displaced children and closed more than 2,000 schools (BATCH-0020-E009; BATCH-0010-E003; BATCH-0022-E008; BATCH-0022-E010). Conflict, armed groups, regional tensions, donor shortages, and inherited state weakness constrain attribution, but the government’s continued state of siege was associated with worsening civilian protection and rights conditions, while state forces were implicated in the August 2023 Goma massacre, including killings, injuries and arbitrary arrests (BATCH-0012-R03-E004; BATCH-0011-E018). Overall, the supplied record supports limited sectoral and institutional gains, but not a demonstrated durable improvement in ordinary people’s life chances across the period.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0012-R01-E019","BATCH-0014-E004","BATCH-0023-E001","BATCH-0009-E004","BATCH-0011-E006"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0020-E005","BATCH-0028-E020","BATCH-0020-E009","BATCH-0010-E003","BATCH-0022-E008","BATCH-0022-E010","BATCH-0012-R03-E004","BATCH-0011-E018"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The supplied evidence does not provide a consistent 2019-to-2023, group-disaggregated outcome series across health, education quality, income, nutrition, housing, water and sanitation.","Several positive indicators are outputs or enrollment measures rather than demonstrated durable outcomes; recast them as attributable or government-linked implementation outputs with explicit limitations.","Removed free maternity care as a completed end-period outcome and retained only its September 2023 launch, noting that the reported benefits cover the subsequent year.","Added the tenure comparison on currency depreciation, near-doubling acute food insecurity, persistent extreme poverty, displacement, low preschool attendance and more than 7.5 million children out of school.","Preserved contrary evidence on food insecurity, displacement, inflation, schooling disruption, the state of siege and the Goma massacre while narrowing causal claims to the supplied attribution."],"reasons_to_reopen_full_ledger":["A full rejudgment would benefit from comparable baseline and end-period household, poverty, nutrition, mortality, schooling-quality and group-disaggregated data.","Independent verification of reported service outputs and completed PDL-145T infrastructure is needed to assess durability and reach.","Further evidence is needed to separate national welfare trends caused by government policy from conflict, donor activity, demographic change and other external shocks."]}
